claims.sentence: <jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title><jats:p>Meta‐analysis of randomized studies on the use of low‐dose aspirin in women at high risk of preeclampsia (PE) has demonstrated that if treatment is initiated at ≤16 weeks' gestation, there is significant reduction in the risk of PE [relative risk (RR) 0.47, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.36-0.62], fetal growth restriction (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.33-0.64), preterm birth (RR 0.35, 95% CI 0.22-0.57) and perinatal death (RR 0.41, 95% CI 0.19-0.92), whereas the effect of treatment after 16 weeks is substantially less (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.61-0.99; RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.88-1.08; RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.97; and RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.73-1.19, respectively).
